chunks: Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Faddal, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿid, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ʿAmmar al-Sabati, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about the beetle, the fly, the locust, the ant, and the like of that, dying in a well, oil, ghee, and similar things. He said: Everything that has no blood, there is no harm in it.

key_terms.الذُّبَابِ: the fly, cited among creatures discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الزَّيْتِ: oil, a liquid to which the ruling applies
key_terms.السَّمْنِ: ghee, another substance covered by the ruling
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well, one of the substances or locations into which such creatures may fall
key_terms.الْجَرَادِ: the locust, included in the examples asked about
key_terms.الْخُنْفَسَاءِ: the beetle mentioned as an example of a small creature falling into liquids
key_terms.بَأْسَ: harm or objection, negated here to indicate permissibility or lack of problem
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood, specifically the presence or absence of blood as the basis of the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if insects without flowing blood die in a well, oil, or ghee?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding small creatures that die in water, oil, ghee, and similar substances. The ruling states that whatever does not have flowing blood does not cause a problem in such cases, making this an important text in discussions of taharah and impurity laws.
